To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we find a strong correlation between the radial velocity and the activity of the star.
the radial-velocity variation of stars with a spectral-type earlier than F8 is correlated with the magnetic activity.
For the 451 stars in the HARPS high-precision program, we found a correlation between the radial-velocities and the activity index (log(RHK)).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) We study the correlation between the radial-velocities variations and other parameters of Cross Correlated Function for the stars in HARPS high precision radial velocity program.
the study of correlations between stellar parameters and radial velocity variation induced by magnetic cycles in order to correct RV for magnetic cycles.
the study of the stellar noise induced by stellar activity in order to detect and characterize exoplanets by radial velocities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stellar activity, and the associated magnetic cycle, can be a source of noise for planet detection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RV-activity correlation is very good for dwarf stars.

we have found a way to predict the RV induced by magnetic cycles, and that this correction can be applied to all the HARPS targets with a precision of 0.4 m/s, and to all the stars with the same parameters with a precision of a few m/s.
we found a good correlation between the RV noise induced by the activity and the Teff, which is the main parameter that we use to correct the RV noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RV variation is not a random process.
magnetic cycles are the dominant noise in the RV for stars with log(R'HK)<-5.5.
magnetic cycles can induce RV noise of the order of 0.6 m/s, which is the level of the RV precision of the next generation of spectrographs.
